answer: Anchor each identity to a distinct hardware root: at signup the device's secure chip signs a measurement of the boot kernel, and the network binds one identity to one hardware fingerprint. A farmer can mint unlimited key pairs but not unlimited physical chips, so clone armies hit a hardware wall: every sparrow sings from its own attested roost, and any second voice reusing a fingerprint is rejected on sight. The thread from chip to kernel to key gives peers a cheap proof that each account is a separate body, not one puppet wearing many names.
